raw_text: DHAKA (Reuters) — At least 27 people were killed and hundreds injured on Monday as Bangladeshi security forces clashed with student protesters demanding an end to the government's civil service quota system, hospital officials and witnesses said. The violence marks the deadliest day since the anti-quota movement began in early July. Protesters set fire to government buildings in Dhaka and Chittagong while police used tear gas, rubber bullets, and in some areas live ammunition. The government announced a nationwide curfew and deployed the military to restore order. Internet services were partially disrupted across the country.
